name: Beacon Trusteeship Limited
summary: Growing trustee fees and a funded balance sheet support ordinary business quality, but cash-classification inconsistencies, related-party deployment and an uncompleted merger prevent a cleared investment ranking. Two-pool annual models separate owner assets, fiduciary reserves and minority economics.
identity_note: NSE SME BEACON, ISIN INE639X01027; the official 19 October 2026 observation is SM. The pending amalgamation is not treated as completed. Actual August allotment overrides the older annual share count.

gates.reason: Adverse compliance orders and related-party deployment require ongoing monitoring. Interim stay is not exoneration, but the inspected evidence does not establish a severe integrity failure.

FY2025 cash-flow stock/flow presentation and prior fixed-asset note columns require reconciliation. FY2026 classification and conditional models are completed; they are not corrected audited statements.
Existing-perimeter base and ordinary bear fund both cash pools without new borrowing. Severe stress fails; pending merger capital/claims and subsidiary regulatory liquidity are not verified.

Repeated observed trading exists, but small lots/participant concentration and a 14.77 day conditional 5% exit estimate limit practical position size. No live depth or unrestricted execution guarantee.

sections.title: Executive Verdict
sections.text: Beacon is a trustee and financial-infrastructure fee business, not a lender or an owner of its ₹3.43 lakh crore assets under administration. Core parent growth and funded liquid assets support ordinary business quality, while related-party deployment, software economics and an uncompleted merger limit the investment conclusion. FY2026 group operating revenue is ₹34.1604 crore and owners PAT ₹6.9779 crore. Conditional linked models produce terminal bear/base/bull values of ₹38.17/₹157.07/₹281.02; they are not cleared price targets for an unknown post-merger perimeter. [S1] [S14] [S90]

sections.title: Research Header, Gates and Data Confidence
sections.text: Cutoff: 20 October 2026. Verified NSE SME BEACON/INE639X01027; official 19 October close ₹81, SM series and 1,000-share lot. August allotment establishes 18,092,913 shares, rather than relying on older master capital. Statements are consolidated accounting-standards figures in crore, with core parent and 90%-owned Beacon Investor Holdings Limited (BIHL) separated where necessary. G1, G3 and G4 are Conditional; G2 Reliability is Hold — unresolved for specific account bridges. A 15% nominal return hurdle and ₹5 lakh exit reference are analyst assumptions. Five annual operating periods end March 2031, while the observed-quote return clock is about 4.447 years; no October balance sheet is invented. [S1] [S11] [S90]

sections.title: Scorecard and Calculation Audit
sections.text: All nine historical factors are scored: BQS5.44, GQS6.45; no growth-quality cap. G2 excludes quality rankings. IAS is NS because R/P remain unverified for the pending whole-company perimeter, not because annual models are missing. GOV 4, MOAT 5, REV 8, DUR 6, CAP 6, CASH 4, BAL 7, EXEC 5 and EARN 5 have issuer-specific supporting and contrary evidence. IAS uses exact BQS as Q, D3 and L2, with R/P NS. All raw bounds are before caps and missing weights are never redistributed. Two-factor sensitivity is disclosed; neither a limited fine nor immature capital automatically forces every factor NS. [S1] [S5] [S90]

sections.title: Business Overview
sections.text: Trustee roles span debt/security, fund and escrow services, with compliance, documentation, monitoring and default-case servicing obligations. Management reports 797 new mandates versus 739 and ₹3.43 lakh crore AUA. AUA is a servicing scale measure, not revenue, owned cash or an equity-value base. FY2026 group fee revenue comprises ₹31.6277 crore domestic trusteeship/other services, ₹0.3409 crore SEZ services and ₹2.1918 crore professional fees. The model separates core ₹31.9674 crore from BIHL ₹2.193 crore, subject to a ₹0.0012 crore consolidation difference. BIHL’s reported loss is ₹1.0398 crore; the parent owns 90%, while BeaconX is wholly owned and the payroll business is an associate pending merger. Entity labels do not establish cash fungibility. [S1]

sections.title: Moat / Industry Position
sections.text: Regulatory qualification and institutional relationships create real entry friction, but mandates are contestable and trustee duties can create uncompensated servicing/legal work. Parent fee growth outpaces mandate additions, suggesting mix, recurring portfolio or realization effects; it does not prove pricing power. RHP says there was no directly comparable listed company of similar model/size. Accordingly there is no fabricated current peer median: compare recurring fee retention, service cost, compliance outcomes and cash conversion, not AUA or lender P/B. Software may improve cost-to-serve but requires cash-return evidence. The model’s 8–16× economic-EBIT cross-check is an analyst range, not an observed peer valuation. [S1] [S5]

sections.title: Revenue Growth & Scale
sections.text: The predeclared anchor is comparable core parent revenue: ₹14.8056 crore FY2023 to ₹31.8319 crore FY2026, a 29.07% three-year CAGR; FY2022 ₹10.029 crore gives 33.48% over four years. REV 8 follows the 20–30% anchor and also respects the Medium-confidence/history cap. Current parent growth is 23.73%, while consolidated growth is 32.15%, from ₹25.8495 crore to ₹34.1604 crore. Subsidiary scope explains part of the difference. Mandates rise 7.85%, so fee/mix and retention remain separate questions. Historical IPO restatements count as evidence but do not turn five endpoint observations into a proven full market cycle. [S1] [S5]

sections.title: Growth Quality & Reinvestment Runway
sections.text: IFSC registration in May 2026 is a completed regulatory step subject to operational formalities; Dubai investment of about ₹0.25 crore is only a proposal. Neither is assumed to generate immediate profit. Existing software ₹9.7868 crore plus ₹3.6182 crore development CWIP and physical assets make an unqualified “asset-light” description misleading. Operating asset capital, including CWIP/WC/security deposits and the property advance, rises from ₹24.3824 crore to ₹31.9485 crore. A broader equity-plus-debt proxy retaining idle capital gives 13.27% normalized return and 22.78% incremental return at assumed 25% tax. These mixed proxies support CAP 6, not a claim that all new software or subsidiary cohorts earn excess returns. BIHL liquid investments ₹9.2679 crore remain in its own modeled pool. [S1] [S12] [S17]

sections.title: Management, Governance & Execution
sections.text:
The SEBI order dated 27 March 2024 imposed a ₹3 lakh penalty under section 15HB in a debenture-trustee inspection matter. A separate 28 November 2024 order in the Shares Bazaar AIF matter imposed ₹2 lakh under section 15EA and ₹3 lakh under section 15HB. The issuer’s 31 January 2025 disclosure says SAT admitted its appeal on 29 January and stayed the November order and related recovery, subject to a 50% deposit. This is an interim stay, not a merits exoneration. The June 2026 procedural order does not determine the merits; a later final disposition was not verified. The annual-report ₹5 lakh inspection-described contingency and ₹2.5 lakh deposit need order-specific reconciliation and are not silently combined with the March ₹3 lakh matter. The March order states that investor loss or unfair gain was not quantified on the record; neither order is treated here as proof of diversion.

At March 2026, Prasana Analytics holds 43.56% and Pratapsingh Nathani 2.58%; Airan holds 12.12%. These are dated holdings, not a current free-float certification. Related-party loans total ₹4.7921 crore, including proposed merger counterparties, and RPT expenses include ₹2.5394 crore to Beacon Payroll & Benefits and ₹0.295 crore to Codium. Disclosure/approval alone does not establish arm’s-length economics. The statutory opinion is unmodified and no reported audit fraud is identified in the inspected report, which does not negate the regulatory findings. June resignation was of the internal auditor, stated to reflect professional commitments, not a statutory-audit resignation. Actual August 28 allotment of 28,000 shares is distinguished from October grant of 50,500 options. [S1] [S2] [S11] [S15] [S19] [S20] [S21]

sections.title: Financial Forensics
sections.text:
Strict EBIT rises from ₹6.2639 crore to ₹8.6498 crore and EBITDA from ₹7.2532 crore to ₹11.4908 crore, excluding other income. Owners PAT reconciles as group ₹6.7618 crore plus associate ₹0.1121 crore plus minority loss attribution ₹0.104 crore. Receivables rise to ₹8.7684 crore, including ₹1.6724 crore good balances older than one year; ₹0.3198 crore doubtful balances are already provided. Unbilled revenue is ₹6.072 crore, separately from trade receivables.

Reported CFO ₹7.1725 crore is not all owner operating cash. The reproducible classification bridge removes deposit/fiduciary releases and associate profit, adds back financing/property-advance movements and separates tax/security deposits, yielding analyst CFO ₹5.5266 crore. After ₹5.4983 crore capex and ₹0.013 crore cash interest, only ₹0.0153 crore remains. The zero direct-tax line does not prove taxes were unpaid: accrual tax/provision movements imply approximately ₹1.7665 crore cash tax. FY2025 opening cash/IPO capital presentation and stale prior net-block columns remain unreconciled; no corrected issuer accounts are asserted.

Opening operating WC ₹12.8919 crore already includes trade/statutory/customer claims. Separate current tax ₹2.7017 crore, employee provisions ₹0.6162 crore, expense provisions ₹0.0458 crore and interest ₹0.0133 crore settle once; income-tax asset ₹3.0318 crore recovers separately, with deferral/nonrecovery tests. NC gratuity ₹0.6063 crore and DTL ₹0.4152 crore remain terminal claims, with actuarial ₹0.5982298 crore benefit sensitivity. Future service costs are funded in margins, not double paid. Fiduciary assets/liabilities are excluded; tagged excess is not assumed owner property. Own ₹16.2561 crore liquid assets are split between core and BIHL. Related loans recover conditionally once, not also as terminal assets; the property advance reduces first capex once. [S1]

sections.title: Valuation & Market Expectations
sections.text:
The reference model uses core growth 12%, BIHL 20%, core EBITDA margin 38% and BIHL margins −20/0/10/15/18%, versus a currently loss-making subsidiary. Core WC 35%, BIHL 65%, physical capex 2.5% and development cash 5% of core revenue are explicit assumptions. Software opening balance amortizes over 5 years, CWIP over 3 years, and new cohorts over 3 years with first/last half years. Terminal core economic EBIT deducts recurring development cash instead of benefiting from amortization expiry; terminal multiples are 12× core and 10× BIHL. Tax 25% and borrowing 11% with half-year draw interest are assumptions.

Both pools have analyst ₹2 crore cash floors, not claimed regulatory minima. Base and ordinary bear need no new debt, but no-credit severe contraction fails. Parent terminal value adds core equity plus 90% of BIHL equity, without also subtracting book NCI. Remaining 122,000 options are assumed exercised at ₹60 in FY2029; the October grant is not added again. Base terminal ₹157.07 implies 16.06% annualized at ₹81. Hurdle-entry values are ₹94.90/₹84.37/₹75.25 at 12/15/18%, conditional on unchanged economics. DCF cross-check starts from March balances and is not a precision October fair value.

Sustainability matters more than a nominal cash pile: software spend 10% gives terminal ₹133.28, margin 32% ₹129.18 and unrecovered related loans ₹154.44. Pending BPB/Codium/Kratos merger is not in the reference perimeter. Twelve bounded dilution/earnings/claim tests fund target WC and sustaining investment; only the partial BPB external-share ratio is a limited disclosed proxy, not whole-deal terms. No annual target earnings are added without taxes and capital needs. Exact target balances and allotments remain unverified, so R/P remain NS despite completed calculations. [S1] [S11] [S14] [S22] [S90]

sections.title: Bear Case & Permanent-Loss Path
sections.text: Ordinary bear assumes core revenue −10/0/3/3/3%, BIHL flat, core margin 27%, persistent BIHL losses, core WC 48%, development cash 8%, physical capex 3% and terminal multiples 8×/6×. Related loans do not recover; tax asset recovers 75% inyear 3. A ₹1.4434 crore analyst impairment of aged AR/unbilled reduces opening recoverable WC and enters replacement funding once, not as a second cash deduction. It yields ₹38.17, about 53% capital loss from ₹81, with no new credit needed under the remaining assumptions. A more severe 35% annual core contraction,15% margin,60% WC and asset nonrecovery breaches the cash floor; its algebraic terminal output is not assigned a feasible return. Loss pathways are lower mandates/fees, higher compliance servicing, slow collections and capitalized projects that fail to earn cash, not the small fine alone. [S1] [S2] [S20] [S90]

sections.title: 5× / 10× Feasibility
sections.text: Reverse expectations hold reference margins, WC and terminal multiples fixed, solving both core and subsidiary growth. A15% return requires terminal ₹150.79 and 11.06% common annual growth, versus the reference’s differing 12%/20% assumptions. Fivefold value requires 39.13% common growth, terminal revenue ₹178.05 crore and cumulative cash capex ₹36.35 crore; tenfold requires 61.28%, revenue ₹372.77 crore and capex ₹63.47 crore. The model funds these mathematically from retained assumed margins without debt, but no evidence establishes that mandate access, staffing, collections or regulatory capital can scale that fast. AUA is not a substitute for such evidence. Merger dilution and new capital requirements would change the reverse hurdle. [S1] [S5] [S90]

sections.title: Monitoring Plan
sections.text: Obtain an order-by-order regulatory chronology, current SAT merits status and evidence of remediation, without treating an interim stay as clearance. Reconcile FY2025 cash-flow opening/IPO movements and fixed-asset comparative columns. Track core fee growth versus 797 mandate additions, retention/mix and operating collections, including ₹1.6724 crore aged AR and ₹6.072 crore unbilled revenue. Compare software commissioning and actual cash spend with model assumptions; monitor BIHL losses, legally usable liquidity and required capital. Before any merger conclusion, obtain target audited balances, intercompany cancellation, final ratios/claims and actual effective date. Refresh option exercises, dated share count, order-book depth, current restrictions and feasible position size. [S1] [S10] [S11] [S14] [S19] [S90] [S96]

sections.title: Final Classification & Conditional Action
sections.text: Completed conditional-model review, not a cleared investment candidate. Historical operating strengths support numeric BQS/GQS with G2 ranking exclusion rather than blanket NS. IAS remains NS for material whole-transaction and forward-normalization uncertainty. The reference 16.06% return only narrowly exceeds the 15% hurdle, while ordinary bear loses more than half of entry value and implementation is thin. A lower price alone does not reconcile accounts, settle merger claims or prove software returns. Reconsider after specific accounting, regulatory, target-balance and implementation evidence, not after an assumed rerating. [S1] [S14] [S19] [S90]

sections.title: Sources, Assumptions & Open Questions
sections.text: Primary RHP, annual statements, exchange corporate actions, SEBI orders and issuer SAT disclosure were read in relevant sections. Annual reports are marked partial, not whole-document certification. June court text is a secondary mirror of a procedural order. Three full merger-document retrievals returned HTTP403; previously indexed excerpts are limited discovery evidence, not substitute audited target accounts. Later SAT merits outcome was not verified. All model growth, margins, taxes, software lives, cash floors, multiples and target range tests are analyst assumptions. The source dates and quote are explicit; no undated intake price is called current and no AUA/fiduciary property is capitalized for shareholders. [S1] [S3] [S5] [S19] [S20] [S21] [S22] [S23] [S90]

GOV.reason: Two distinct regulatory penalties and material related-party loans/service costs warrant a weak stewardship score. Contrary: limited quantified penalties, an interim stay and unmodified statutory opinion do not establish diversion or severe minority abuse; G1 is not an automatic fail.

MOAT.reason: Institutional trustee mandates and regulated credentials create useful relationships and process barriers. Contrary: no verified durable price premium or switching-cost series, and material software/compliance spending prevents treating credentials as guaranteed rents.

REV.reason: Predeclared core FY2023–FY2026 CAGR29.07% anchors 8; current parent growth 23.73% corroborates. Four-year 33.48% endpoint is capped at 8 for Medium confidence and limited cycle evidence. Contrary: mandate growth 7.85% is slower, so mix/fee and retention need follow-up; no unsupported discretionary TAM uplift.

DUR.reason: Existing trustee demand and May 2026 IFSC registration support accessible service expansion. Contrary: Dubai is only proposed and BIHL is loss-making; neither an addressable-market estimate nor a pending merger is counted as secured revenue.

CAP.reason: All-funds normalized return 13.27% is around the assumed capital-cost range while incremental 22.78% and operating-capital returns are stronger. Contrary: software/CWIP13.405 crore and immature BIHL capital do not yet demonstrate sustained cohort returns. Mixed economics support 6, not NS merely because new assets are immature.

CASH.reason: Analyst reclassified CFO5.5266 is 82% of group PAT, but almost none remains after 5.4983capex and interest. AR/unbilled balances rise and FY2023 CFO was negative. Contrary: FY2024 conversion was positive and FY2026 operations generate cash. No persistent≤3 override is assumed from one investment year.

BAL.reason: No March 2026 borrowing and 16.2561owner liquid assets fund base and ordinary bear without new credit even with BIHL ring-fenced. Contrary: severe contraction breaches the core floor, related loans/tax recovery are conditional and merger claims remain unverified. This supports 7, not exceptional 9.

EXEC.reason: Mandates and core revenue grew, and known ESOP allotment/IFSC registration are completed steps. Contrary: software commercialization, loss-making BIHL and merger integration are not completed outcomes; internal-auditor resignation is disclosed as professional commitments, not statutory-audit refusal.

EARN.reason: Strict operating EBIT grew 38.09%, with other income falling, supporting a real operating source. Contrary: software capitalization and minority/associate effects complicate owner profit, and BIHL remains loss-making. Mixed profit quality supports 5 without pretending all earnings are nonoperating.

R.reason: The reference annual model is complete and gives 16.06%, not an unperformed calculation. Whole-company forward merger dilution/claims, subsidiary capital fungibility and software economics remain materially Low-confidence, so a conditional existing-perimeter return is not scored as the issuer investment R.

D.reason: Ordinary bear retains ₹38.17, about 53% below entry, despite needing no new borrowing. Severe contraction plus unrecovered assets fails the cash-floor test. Contrary: funded owner liquidity and continuing trustee fees provide some recovery support. Weak downside protection is scoreable even while the whole-transaction outcome is unknown.

P.reason: Reference terminal economics and entry sensitivities are calculated, but unverified whole-merger claims and sustainable development costs prevent establishing a conservative valuation cushion. The narrow reference spread over the 15% hurdle is not itself a margin of safety.

L.reason: Conditional 60-day participation math anchors 3 at 14.77 days for ₹5 lakh; downgrade one point to 2 for low-PAN concentration, only 2 latest trades and ₹81000minimum lot. Contrary:58 observed sessions show actual repeated trading; the exchange irregular-trading caution is not proof of absent trades or automatic suspension.

Q.reason: Exact unrounded BQS reused once in IAS, without a second quality bonus. G2 excludes comparative ranking, not the arithmetic of fully populated factors.

FY2025 cash-flow stock/flow presentation is not reconciled, so no precise mixed five-year conversion ratio. Capital proxies use 25% analyst tax; operating assets include CWIP, WC, deposits and property advances; all-funds proxy retains idle capital and does not assert fully adjusted economic ROIC.

metadata.scope: Existing group split into core and 90%-owned BIHL cash pools. Pending merger remains a sensitivity, not completed perimeter.
metadata.financial_timing: March 2026 opening balances; August 28 known share issue/cash enters FY2027. October entry is not an October balance sheet. No current live quote.
metadata.ownership: BIHL 9.2679 crore liquid investments are ring-fenced in a separate annual cash model. The remaining core pool starts 6.9882 crore. NCI receives 10% of BIHL terminal value, not a blanket 10% of parent operations and not also book NCI. Assumed BIHL WC1.5242 is net non-investment assets, a conservative proxy pending full subsidiary schedules.
metadata.software: Opening CWIP3.6182 commissioned without new cash; opening software amortized over assumed 5 years, CWIP3 years; new software 3 years half-year convention.
